title: Resurrection and Justification
english: We are burdened with the weight of sin from our ancient transgressions.
The prophet declares that the Lord was pleased with his land and forgave the iniquities of his people, covering all their sins.
This beatitude applies to both the circumcised and the Gentiles, as Paul explains in his letter to the Romans.
We are justified in Christ, who was handed over for our transgressions and raised for our justification.
If Christ was not raised, then those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
But the prophet assures us that the dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, each receiving the reward they deserve.
God is the judge of all, and now Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
The first man, Adam, fell into sin and became the beginning of those who slipped into corruption, and death came into the world through him.
Just as Adam was the first to fall, so too will all people be justified through the resurrection of the dead, which comes through a man, Jesus Christ.
The mystery of the divine economy is revealed in the fact that it was necessary for a man to conquer death on our behalf, and this is precisely what the Word of God, who became man, accomplished.
He did not take the form of angels but of the seed of Abraham, so that he might be like his brothers in all things.
In this way, he was able to heal the fallen and to overcome death through obedience and righteousness, which is the opposite of the transgression and sin that led to death.
The Son of God, who did not know sin, became man, so that just as all were condemned in Adam, so all might be justified in Christ and put off the death that came from sin.
As the apostle Paul says, 'just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.' (Romans 5:19)
Through our transgressions, Christ was given over to death, but for our justification, he was raised to life.
As a result, we who are in him have also been raised to new life.
The Word of God, which is life itself, has been bestowed not just on Christ's physical body, but on the entirety of human nature.
Christ, as the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, has been raised from the dead, and in due time, the rest of humanity will also be brought to life.
However, this resurrection will not occur in a chaotic or disorderly manner, but rather in a way that is both organized and discerning, with each person being raised in their proper time.

title: Supremacy of Saints in Christ
english: The saints who lived after the incarnation, having fallen asleep in faith, are superior to those who lived before. For although there were undoubtedly saints in Israel during the time of the law, with the law-given life being praised and still prevailing, those in Christ are better. They have been justified through faith and have become partakers of the divine nature, enriched with the spirit of adoption. As a result, they have been called into brotherhood by the grace of the natural and true Son.

In contrast to the spirit of slavery that existed among those under the law, we cry out 'Abba, Father' (Romans 8:15). This indicates that those in Christ are indeed better than the ancients. Our Lord Jesus Christ also implies this in the evangelical parables, where he says that the householder hires workers into the vineyard and pays them their wages, starting from the last to the first (Matthew 20:8-16). This will occur when he hands over the kingdom to God and the Father, abolishing all authority and power and might. At that time, the Son himself will also be subjected to the one who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all (1 Corinthians 15:28).

Some people attempt to belittle the Son by saying that he hands over the kingdom to the Father and submits to him as an inferior. However, it must be said that the Son endured a voluntary emptiness, becoming like us and humbling himself from his lofty heights, while remaining conformed and equal to the Father. He is currently hidden in God, but he will be revealed in all his glory at the time of the completion of the present age, now sitting at the right hand of the Father.

If the Son were to be brought down from his current glory, would he not undergo a second emptiness? And if he were to hand over the kingdom, how could he come with the holy angels in the glory of his Father (Matthew 25:31)? Has not the Son been given the task of putting his enemies under his feet (1 Corinthians 15:25), for now he reigns with the Father, but then he would fall from the kingdom. Nevertheless, even if the Son submits to the Father, he is not inferior to him, for submission is not a limit of nature or essence, but rather indicates a manner of action. If this were to happen among us who are not of a different essence, it would not prove difference, for a son submits to a father, a slave to a master, a student to a teacher, and someone to a leader; yet none of this injures the argument of co-essence, for they are like each other and even if they have this manner of submission, they honor each other and do not dishonor each other for the sake of harmony.

Therefore, how can they prevail over God if we are weak? For if being subject to the Son is a natural property or a measure, as they claim, then not being subject must be a property of a different nature, possibly one that is even better, given that submission is associated with lesser things. This is because he submits to God economically, for our sake.

The one who spoke in this way explained that since humanity had sinned and become subject to corruption, the devil, and demons, having departed from God by nature, the Only-Begotten became human for our sake. He abolished the power of death, removed the root of death, which is sin, and cast out the ruler of this age. Having accomplished all this and completed the entire economy, he will hand over the kingdom that was stolen long ago by others to the Father.

title: Resurrection
english: When all things on earth have been restored to their rightful state, with death and Satan, who tyrannized over them, having been rendered powerless, the Son will again have the superiority of authority over all things in the future age.

The prophet Isaiah prophesies beforehand, saying that the dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, and those on the earth will rejoice, for the dew from God is a healing for them, symbolizing the life-giving energy of God, by which he grants being to non-beings and well-being to those already existing (Isaiah 26:19).
All things consist in God, just as they were also brought into being through him.

David also sings about the things on earth to the Savior God of all, saying that when God opens his hand, all things will be filled with goodness, but when he turns away his face, they will be troubled; you will take away their spirit, and they will fail, and they will return to their dust; you will send out your spirit, and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth (Psalm 104:29-30).

Human nature suffered the turning away of the divine face in Adam due to transgression, and therefore, it has been almost completely destroyed and troubled, and it has returned to its own dust, and it has been led down to death and corruption.
With the Only-Begotten Word of God dwelling among us and the Holy Spirit's presence enriching our lives, we are undergoing a transformation, returning to our original state and being rebuilt.
This is because we have been called to a new life, one that escapes the power of death.

The apostle Paul, in his wisdom, testifies to this truth, saying that if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in us, He will give life to our mortal bodies through His Spirit dwelling in us (Romans 8:11).
When Christ rose from the dead, conquering the power of death and becoming the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, it is only logical that we will follow in His footsteps.

If someone were to carefully examine the works of God and the origin of each thing, seeking to thoroughly understand the manner of each creation and the beginning of each generation, they would never finish asking how this is possible.
For instance, one might wonder how heaven was made, from what material or where, what foundation it has, or how the earth was created and divided, or how the sun, moon, and stars were formed.
Similarly, the creation of humanity is a profound mystery, as it involves the transformation of dust into flesh and bones.
If we cannot understand the reason behind each of these creations, we risk abolishing the fact that they were created at all.
Doubting the resurrection after Christ's resurrection is a sign of foolishness, ignorance, and arrogance, as it questions the power of God's works.
Asking how God's works are done or with what body the dead will rise is also foolish.
Some people claim that the soul preexisted and was bound to the body as a form of punishment, but this idea undermines the concept of creation and the purpose of God's work.

The Lord rose from the dead in the same body, as the prophet Isaiah said, 'The dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, and those on the earth will rejoice; for the dew from you is a healing for them' (Isaiah 26:19).

As David said, 'When you open your hand, all things will be filled with goodness; but when you turn away your face, they will be troubled; you will take away their spirit, and they will fail, and they will return to their dust; you will send out your spirit, and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth' (Psalm 104:29-30).
Paul also said, 'If the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in us, He will give life to our mortal bodies through His Spirit dwelling in us' (Romans 8:11).
